On the walk toward the east market, I practiced the side step every time nobody was close enough to see.

Small.

Just leave the line.

Again.

Better.

Again.

My right foot wanted too much distance.

Again.

By the third street I was starting to think I had it.

Then a vegetable cart appeared in the part of the world I had temporarily stopped paying attention to.

I nearly walked straight into it.

The merchant made his opinion of me available to the entire block.

I stopped.

Looked at the cart.

Looked at my feet.

Right.

The world got a vote.

I kept going.

Two things.

Overhead cut.

Side step.

Money first.

Then everything else.

I practiced until the light went bad.

Cut straight.

Step small.

Again.

The strange thing was that two things were enough to occupy an entire body.

My mind kept offering improvements.

My shoulder kept reminding me about the shale.

My hands kept reminding me about the bucket.

Antonius had seven days left on my clock.

Arlo had one result worth repeating.

The cart existed somewhere behind a masonry stall, charging me rent for being a pile of rocks.

Cut straight.

Step small.

Again.

Eventually darkness won.

On the walk home, without asking permission, my brain began calculating how much gambling capital I would need to clear Antonius in three nights.

I noticed the thought.

That was something.

I knew enough to recognize it as dangerous.

Also something.

Then the more dangerous part arrived.

I knew enough to make it sound reasonable.

Past Greg had decades of experience.

Current Greg had ten silver worth of debt, a storage bill, bad footwork, and an idea.

Right.

That was going to be a problem.

I smiled.

Sella saw the expression.

"What now?"

Potentially expensive progress.

She sighed like the answer had confirmed something unfortunate.

I put the silver in my pocket.

My burned coat smelled worse every second.

My wrist hurt.

Recovery had become tomorrow's training problem.

Vale expected money in two days.

Jorren would be gone north next week.

Arlo had apparently moved the project forward without me.

The world had not waited while I learned two things.

Good.

I went to see what it had done.

Tonight, I had a partner.

A filtration process worth eight copper.

Eight copper.

A coat with an acid hole in it.

Enough money to become poor honestly again by morning.

And one newly verified fact about myself.

Being smarter had not removed the idiot.

No.

It had given him better arguments.

And a bypass.

He nodded.

The dyer had become part of the experiment whether either of us liked it or not.

Also good.

I sat on the repaired stool and looked at my hand again.

One pulse.

One crooked shimmer.

Enough to move liquid for less than a second.

My sword had taken a month to become mine.

Maybe mana would take longer.

Maybe much longer.

That hurt more than the sword had.

Swordsmanship was something I had respected.

Support was what I had become.

There are failures that tell you what you cannot do.

This one had done something worse.

It reminded me what I wanted back.

Outside, someone rolled a cart through the alley.

The wheel hit a stone and rattled.

Arlo started measuring clay.

I had almost no money.

Jorren left north soon.

Our first customer wanted a refund, a repair, and possibly another filter.

My old magic existed in my body as approximately one badly shaped breath.

Progress.

Apparently.

## Chapter-specific listening guardrail

> **TIME MUST LEAVE RESIDUE.**

The listener should hear that absence had consequences. Jorren moved farther north. Greg's body and habits changed. Sella became more efficient with him. Arlo and Ivena redesigned, tested, negotiated, sold, and financed work without waiting for Greg. Greg returns to a life that continued moving.

The exact spoken transcript, ordered source boundaries, provider artifact identities, and deterministic take order live in `greg-again/audio/takes/011.json`. The 29 takes are production seams only. They exist because the currently available raw provider artifact path is the short-take path; they do not change story wording or story state.
